new_issues.title: Item resume applies the implementation dependency check (dependency must be cf-complete) to tasks-plan items, so a retried tasks item with an unimplemented dependency is flagged without running.
new_issues.why: _cf_slices_needing_tasks builds items with _slice_item, which reads the design's dependencies, and _resume_locked runs _open_dependencies for every pipeline, flagging any in-plan dependency whose cf status is not complete. A fresh tasks-plan batch never requires dependencies to be implemented (design: a task batch does not build on its dependencies' output), and the design says item resume works on tasks-plan runs with no pipeline-specific code, so retrying a tasks-plan item whose dependency is only designed returns FLAGGED 'dependency N not complete' and cannot proceed until the dependency is implemented. slices-plan items are unaffected (undesigned slices have no dependencies).

new_issues.title: pipeline_mutates does not walk a fan_out step's 'inner' config, so a fan_out wrapping a mutating step would run without the run lock.
new_issues.why: _step_mutates only recurses into config['steps']; fan_out keeps its nested step under 'inner' and FanOutStep.validate does not restrict the inner type beyond forbidding nested fan_out. True, but no shipped pipeline uses fan_out at all, and a fan_out of a committing phase step (concurrent branches in one checkout) is not a meaningful configuration; same hypothetical class as 197-I9.

new_issues.title: The run lock is per worktree while run state and reports live in the shared ~/.config/squadron/runs, so concurrent resumes of the same run from two worktrees can lose a report update.
new_issues.why: project_run_lock locks {git dir}/squadron-run.flock (per worktree, deliberately) and StateManager defaults to a global runs dir, so two item resumes of one run id from different worktrees each load-modify-write the same report.json. True, but it requires deliberately resuming one batch's items from two different checkouts at once, whose cf integration targets differ; the per-worktree scope is the documented D11 choice.

new_issues.title: A not_run item that is retried and halts is recorded flagged/step_failed, and not_run records carry no flag_kind, so counts under-report.
new_issues.why: BatchReport.count counts by outcome, so not_run counts are correct (the finding concedes this), and not_run having no flag_kind is the designed shape. After a retry the item did run, so recording its real outcome with decision=retry is correct, not lost information. No defect.

new_issues.title: Rewriting the whole report after every item makes total report bytes written quadratic in batch size.
new_issues.why: _write_each_report(final=False) rewrites both files per item, as D7 requires, off the event loop via asyncio.to_thread. Batches are plan-sized (tens of slices) and each item takes minutes of model work, so the cost has no real effect.

new_issues.title: The run lock is taken at two sites (run.py _locked and item_resume.resume_item) with different error rendering.
new_issues.why: run() routes --item to handle_item_resume before any _locked call, and resume_item takes project_run_lock itself, so there is no double acquisition; both refusals exit 2. A structure/duplication point with no behavioral defect.

new_issues.title: A reserved -p key on an item resume is refused through typer.BadParameter with a generic message that does not name the reserved key.
new_issues.why: handle_item_resume calls _apply_param_overrides, which raises typer.BadParameter(reserved_param_error(key)); with no param hint Click renders 'Invalid value: <message>', so the reserved-key message is shown, and the exit code is 2 as D8 requires (the finding concedes the code matches). The claimed defect does not exist.
